title: After The Feast
summary: Thanksgiving Day has been a fully owned subsidiary of the National Football League since the 1960s, and a feature of the schedule since the early '20s, but there is an American tradition older than the Dayton Triangles and Frankford Yellow Jackets, and that's turning on your boss. In other words, Aaron Rodgers stole the weekend before it even started, and thoughtfully if coincidentally, the three teams that Rodgers claimed Mike McCarthy inflicted his narcoleptic cruelties upon, the Green Bay Packers, Dallas Cowboys and Pittsburgh Steelers, featured heavily. Now under normal circumstances, three games like Thursday's would \ stand alone as brilliant entertainments. The three games—Chicago over Detroit, 39-35, Philadelphia over Dallas, 39-38, and Buffalo over Kansas City, 13-10—were decided on a spectacular touchdown catch with three seconds left , a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left to cap a three-touchdown comeback , and a blocked punt that led to a 57-yard field goal in a driving freezing rainstorm with none seconds left. If that doesn't make you forget about your woes, you're just not into ball.

title: We Must Always Remain Thankful For The Dallas Cowboys
summary: This year's slate of Thanksgiving games couldn't have unfolded much better from the perspective of a neutral fan. It was hard not to feel stuffed after just the first game, a 39-35 Bears win over the Lions that featured some of the season's most entertaining football, being played by two of the league's most entertaining teams. How could a game like that possibly be topped? Perhaps with a game that was just as thrilling, featured a 21-point comeback, and provided a healthy dose of schadenfreude. That is what the Eagles and Cowboys delivered in the second game of the day: a purely delightful viewing experience. I am always left with a slight sickly feeling at the end of a game like Bears-Lions, only because it feels unfair for a game so good to have to produce a loser. It just doesn't seem right that Jahmyr Gibbs can carry the ball 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns and not get to spend today as the biggest story in the NFL. This is why the Cowboys are such a valuable presence in the league—they could come out on the losing end of the greatest game of all time and not one person, save for some number of degenerates, would be forced to feel an ounce of sympathy for them. Reasons to delight in the suffering of this franchise are so myriad that everyone can find their own for doing so ( I choose this one ). The Cowboys of recent vintage have become especially adept at delivering the goods to their true constituents, the nation's haters. A team with this purpose must maintain a delicate balance. They can't be so bad as to make all of their games unwatchable, but they can't be good enough to find steady competence. They have to be both an entertaining watch and a squad of self-sabotaging dopes. For a while there, we all had to wait until the playoffs for the Cowboys to make their face-first landing, but now the team has been fine-tuned to meet their true purpose. We can watch the Cowboys eat shit in inventive, entertaining ways just about every week now.
